276.question: In the general model of transition, political modernization means movement...

options.A: From any state to a stateless society
options.B: From a territorial organization to an exclusively kinship-based one
options.C: From traditional structures to more rationally organized ones
options.E: From professional administration to a rejection of institutions

277.question: Modernization that develops gradually through internal processes is called...

278.question: The main feature of secondary modernization is...

options.A: Catch-up development drawing on external experience
options.B: A rejection of political participation by the population
options.C: A mandatory coincidence of reforms with revolution
options.D: The exclusive reproduction of traditional orders
options.E: The absence of contact with more developed societies

279.question: Institutionalization means that organizations and procedures acquire...

options.A: A complete absence of internal rules
options.C: Stability and the capacity to change without being destroyed
options.D: An unchanging personal composition of the leadership
options.E: The ability to replace any rights with personal loyalty

280.question: Processes that are part of political modernization:

options.A: Differentiation and ordering of the functions of power
options.B: Grounding legitimacy mainly in the immutability of a sacred order
options.C: An increased capacity for structural change
options.D: Retaining the former political roles while institutions are formally renewed

281.question: After the earlier ideals have collapsed, citizens cannot determine their belonging to the political community. This is a crisis of...

282.question: The number of people wishing to influence decisions is growing, while the channels of representation remain closed. This is a crisis of...

283.question: The central authority makes decisions, but they are systematically not carried out locally. This is a manifestation of the crisis of...

284.question: The values of the ruling regime diverge from the majority's ideas of just government. This is a crisis of...

285.question: Tension over access to benefits and over the costs of reform belongs primarily to the crisis of...

286.question: The main contradiction of modernization is connected with...

options.A: The absence of differences between traditional and modern society
options.B: The impossibility of combining political participation and institutions
options.C: The mandatory coincidence of any reforms with cultural traditions
options.D: Universal goals of transformation versus national-traditional conditions
options.E: The immutability of social roles under any transformation

287.question: Indicate the measures that can alleviate the crisis of participation.

options.A: Restraining new associations as the main means of institutional renewal
options.B: Preferring appointment to equal access to participation
options.D: Developing the representation of new interests
options.E: Entrenching the former channels of representation regardless of changes in group demands

288.question: Demands are growing rapidly, representation is weak, and the implementation of decisions is deteriorating. Which crises are directly combined here?

options.A: Identity, with no signs of a crisis of participation
options.B: Legitimacy, with no contradictions in representation and implementation
options.E: Distribution, with no signs of a crisis of penetration

289.question: Directions that correspond to overcoming the crises of modernization include...

options.A: Replacing horizontal links with one-way administrative communication
options.B: Unifying organizational forms without assessing their actual stability
options.D: Rational organization of the implementation of decisions
options.E: Centralizing the resolution of local issues without delimiting enforceable powers

290.question: Why does the rapid borrowing of formal institutions not in itself guarantee successful modernization?

options.A: Stable procedures, public consensus-building and attention to local conditions are needed
options.B: Establishing constitutional norms in itself provides the skills of political participation
options.C: The speed with which new norms are adopted is a sufficient indicator of institutional stability
options.D: Agreeing reforms with the opposition is equivalent to preserving the former political functions
options.E: Borrowed forms determine their functions in advance, regardless of the social environment
